answer: The area of water is 0.3052 km², as calculated from the SAR backscatter analysis using a threshold of -16.0 dB. This water extent is concentrated in the northern-western quadrant, which contains 849 water pixels — the dominant quadrant for water detection. The optical water mask (from tools.water_highlight) identified a much larger area (14,705 pixels), but the SAR mask and optical mask disagree significantly, with an IoU of only 0.020048. The SAR-derived water area represents 4.66% of the total image, while the optical mask covers 22.44%. The SDWI metric was not used for masking but was computed for reference. The water pixels identified by SAR are consistent with the dominant quadrant and the northern sector.
